transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today, and what has been bothering you recently?

Lately I keep making really careless mistakes, even on things I know well, and it’s starting to cause problems at work. I’ll miss small details in emails or forms, and then have to redo things because I overlooked something obvious.
Have you had similar problems with attention or careless mistakes since you were a child or teenager (for example in school or at home), or is this a more recent change just in the last few years?

I’ve actually had this kind of problem since I was a kid, especially in school—losing points for small mistakes even when I understood the material. It’s gotten a lot more noticeable and disruptive over the last 10 months or so, but it isn’t completely new.

Over the past few months, have you also noticed periods of feeling unusually sad or low, or very anxious or on edge most days, or is it mainly the attention and careless mistakes that are bothering you?
It’s mainly the attention issues and careless mistakes that are bothering me. I have normal ups and downs, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling persistently sad or highly anxious most days.

Besides the careless mistakes, do you also often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, or find your mind frequently jumping from one thing to another even when you’re trying to focus on a single task?

Physically I’m not especially restless—I can sit still fine and I don’t fidget a lot. The problem is more in my head: my mind jumps to other thoughts or random things I need to do, even when I’m really trying to focus on one task.

Because of these attention problems, how much are your daily life and work actually affected—for example, are you missing deadlines, getting negative feedback, or struggling to keep up with routine tasks at home or work?

Yeah, it’s definitely affecting things. I’ve missed a couple of deadlines or had to ask for extensions because I overlooked details, and my manager has mentioned a few times that I need to be more careful. At home I’ll forget small tasks—like paying a bill or following through on something I said I’d do—unless I write it down right away.

Do you also often find it hard to stay organized or finish tasks you start—for example, frequently leaving projects half-done, misplacing important items like keys or documents, or procrastinating on tasks that need sustained mental effort even when you intend to do them on time?

Yeah, that describes me pretty well. I’ll start projects and then leave them half-finished, and I misplace things like my keys or important papers all the time. I also tend to put off tasks that take a lot of focus, like reports or paperwork, even when I know I should just get them done.

Back in school, did teachers or parents ever say you had specific difficulties with reading, writing, or math (like reading very slowly, frequent spelling mistakes, or trouble understanding numbers), even when you tried hard, or was it more that you understood the work but lost points because of inattention and careless errors?

It was more that I understood the work but lost points because of inattention and careless errors. Teachers would say things like “you know this, you just rush and miss stuff,” and I’d get problems wrong for skipping steps or not reading the instructions carefully, rather than not understanding the material.
Outside of work and school, do you notice these attention and organization problems also affecting you in other areas, like social situations, hobbies, or managing daily errands and appointments?

Yeah, it shows up outside of work too. I’ll zone out in conversations and realize I missed part of what someone said, and I’ve forgotten social plans or appointments unless I put them straight into my phone. Even with hobbies, I’ll get excited, buy what I need, and then never quite organize myself enough to follow through.
Have you ever had a significant head injury, neurological illness, or other medical event after childhood that led to a clear change or worsening in your thinking, attention, or personality?

No, I’ve never had a significant head injury or any neurological illness that I know of. I also don’t recall any specific medical event after childhood that caused a clear change in my thinking or personality.

Do you regularly use alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or any other substances or medications that affect your thinking or energy, and if so, do you notice your attention problems getting clearly better or worse when you use them or when they wear off?

I drink socially on weekends, maybe a couple of drinks, but not enough that I’ve noticed a clear change in my attention one way or the other. I don’t use cannabis or stimulants or anything like that, and I haven’t really noticed substances affecting my focus.
